# Independent audit: actual nine-base weighted graph failure



## 1. Actual convex body and canonical forest

The three displayed triangle inequalities have exactly the nine stated integer solutions. The triangle has area \(13/2\), primitive edges, and six interior lattice points, consistent with the direct enumeration. The minimum of the concave two-plane roof is seven, so all nine continuous fibers remain full-dimensional and positive for every \(R\ge0,d\ge1\).

The simplex-fiber inequality description defines a compact full-dimensional actual body. Taking the hull of its mixed source leaves each integer fiber unchanged and introduces no new integer index. Every fiber has the same intrinsic dimension \(d\), so the mixed measure is precisely the stated sum of \(d\)-volumes.

The parity root ties are resolved exactly by the prescribed base norm rule. The choices do not change with \(R\) or \(d\). All five parent bases and radius identities hold, and each directed path terminates at a designated root. Common homothetic simplex shape upgrades each radius identity to the actual Minkowski set equality.

## 2. Exact weighted graph maximum

The affine substitution \(t=(d+1)x_1-R\) recovers the roof coordinate on every true fiber centroid. The nine normals and thresholds consequently define actual ambient halfspaces whose graph traces are exactly those listed, including every boundary centroid.

For \(R=21,d=1\), the nine closed graph-cap masses are

    35, 70, 69, 35, 70, 35, 68, 59, 28.

Their maximum is 70. The exact midpoint relation \(G_1=(G_0+G_4)/2\), with all three weights equal, gives a matching lower bound at graph point 1. Thus the maximum graph depth is exactly \(70/301=10/43\), with quarter-depth gap \(3/172\).

The same argument is independent of dimension: every displayed cap has at most two atoms, each of weight at most \((R+14)^d\), and the three atoms in the midpoint lower bound have exactly that weight. The common simplex factor \(1/d!\) cancels. This proves the exact formula for all \(R,d\), not merely the asymptotic limit.

For the explicit all-dimensional choice \(R=63d-7\), the finite binomial estimate is valid term by term and its finite geometric sum is strictly below \(9/8\). The resulting inequality

\[
2(R+14)^d<\tfrac94(R+7)^d\le T_d(R)/4
\]

has the correct factors and gives strict graph failure in every continuous dimension. No affine dimension change or omitted fiber is involved.

For comparison, keeping the fixed value \(R=21\) gives graph failure in dimensions one and two, but not in dimensions three and above: after division by \(35^d\), the necessary inequality is

\[
(34/35)^d+(33/35)^d+(31/35)^d+(28/35)^d>3.
\]

Its left side is strictly decreasing in \(d\), is above three at \(d=2\), and below three at \(d=3\). The source avoids this limitation by choosing \(R\) with \(d\).

## 3. Original continuous-volume compensation

Fibers 0,1,4 are identical copies of \(B=(R+14)K\), and their bases form an arithmetic progression. For every nonzero continuous normal at their common centroid, the three thresholds are \(0,s,-s\), after centering in \(B\). Ordinary Grünbaum gives the first \(\Gamma_dV\); the independently proved paired-centroid-tail theorem gives the remaining \(2\Gamma_dV\). These are disjoint actual source fibers.

When the continuous normal is zero, the cap captures the entire middle fiber and at least one endpoint, giving \(2V\ge3\Gamma_dV\). Moving a containing cap through the candidate only decreases its mass. The argument therefore covers all closed ambient caps, including supporting, full, empty, and vertical cases.

The total mass is at most \(9V\). Hence the original depth at that same centroid is at least \(\Gamma_d/3\), strictly above the OC target \(\Gamma_d/4\). This is a full-dimensional simplex-fiber statement for every \(d\), with no use of a central-symmetry property of higher-dimensional simplices.

Only in dimension one is the equal three-fiber block centrally symmetric. Its half-mass argument independently gives \(105/602=15/86>1/8\) for \(R=21\), without the general paired-tail theorem. The source correctly distinguishes these arguments.

The interval row-1 ambient cap is \(2x-z_1\ge33\). Its actual captured lengths sum to \(281/2\), although its graph atom mass is 70. This directly illustrates why the certified graph upper bound cannot be interpreted as an upper bound for the original volume depth.

## 4. Optional exact terminal-face check

The two maximal terminal-root patches have index sets

\[
E=\{0,1,3,4,5\},\qquad F=\{0,2,5,6,7,8\}.
\]

Their projections are triangles with vertices \((0,3,5)\) and \((0,5,8)\), respectively; these index sets are their complete integer sets. Root 1 and root 2 are relatively interior to their respective patches, and the shared graph edge has endpoints 0 and 5. In the interval calibration their masses are 175 and 196, with overlap mass 70.

Both patches have relative Helly number three. Exact enumeration gives no convex-position four-subset in either patch. Empty unimodular triangles \(\{0,1,5\}\) and \(\{2,5,6\}\) give the matching three-set lower witnesses. The finite minimal-family witness argument then proves the upper bound three. Thus the actual graph obstruction is compatible with the proved affine-patch filtration; it also prevents inferring a global cost four by subtracting the shared edge's Helly number two from the separate costs \(3+3\).

The source's conclusion is a definitive failure of the specified weighted centroid-graph selector under actual zero-slack forest geometry. It is not an OC counterexample; it supplies an explicit stronger-than-target original-volume center.
